articles.title: Emergency go bag inventory
articles.summary: Build and maintain a portable collection of essential supplies for a short notice evacuation.
body: Identify each household member’s essential needs, including mobility, communication, medications, and infant or pet supplies.
Choose a bag that each intended carrier can lift and transport safely. Avoid making the bag so heavy that it slows evacuation.
Pack drinking water, shelf stable food, a flashlight, spare batteries, a power bank, basic first aid supplies, hygiene items, and weather appropriate clothing.
Include copies of essential contact information and documents, protected against water and unauthorized access.
Add a paper map, a whistle, and a small amount of cash in appropriate denominations.
Check expiration dates, battery charge, clothing sizes, and changing medical needs on a recurring schedule.
Store the bag in a known accessible location and make sure household members know where it is.

articles.title: Household emergency contact card
articles.summary: Prepare a compact contact and reunification reference that works without a phone.
body: Write the names and phone numbers of primary caregivers, local emergency contacts, and one contact outside the affected region.
Identify a nearby meeting location and a separate location outside the neighborhood, accounting for accessibility needs.
Include relevant medical alert information only when necessary and protect sensitive information from casual disclosure.
Provide each household member with a paper copy appropriate to their age and circumstances.
Agree on a simple procedure for reporting safety and location when communications are available.
Review the card whenever contact numbers, schools, workplaces, or household needs change.

articles.title: Safe flashlight and battery readiness
articles.summary: Maintain safe portable lighting during a power outage.
body: Place a working flashlight or headlamp in each important household location and keep a spare accessible.
Use the battery chemistry and charging equipment specified by the manufacturer.
Inspect battery compartments for corrosion, swelling, leaks, or heat damage. Do not use damaged cells.
Charge rechargeable devices ahead of forecast disruptions and periodically test their operation.
Keep spare batteries in their original packaging or protected holders so terminals cannot short together.
Use battery powered lighting rather than candles where possible to reduce fire risk.
Do not charge damaged lithium ion batteries or leave charging equipment in unsafe locations.

articles.title: Refrigerator and freezer outage log
articles.summary: Track power interruptions and food temperature to support safer food decisions.
body: Record the time the power failed and the last known refrigerator and freezer temperatures if available.
Keep refrigerator and freezer doors closed as much as practical to slow warming.
Use an appliance thermometer to measure temperatures rather than judging food by smell or appearance.
Follow current USDA or local public health guidance for time and temperature limits before deciding whether to keep perishable food.
When in doubt about the safety of perishable food, discard it. Do not taste food to determine safety.
Record when power returned and any food discarded or moved to another safe cold storage location.

articles.title: Boil water advisory response
articles.summary: Respond to an official boil water advisory without confusing it with a do not drink notice.
body: Confirm the exact notice and affected area using the water utility or local public health authority.
Identify whether the notice is a boil water advisory, a do not drink notice, or a do not use notice. Boiling does not remove chemical contaminants.

For a boil water advisory concerning microbial contamination, bring clear water to a full rolling boil for one minute, or three minutes at elevations above 6,500 feet, unless the issuing authority directs otherwise.
If water is cloudy, first filter it through a clean cloth, paper towel, or coffee filter or allow particles to settle and pour off the clear water.
Let boiled water cool in a clean, covered container. Use treated or approved bottled water for drinking, preparing food, and brushing teeth as directed.
Follow the issuing authority’s specific instructions for infant formula, medical devices, dishwashing, and pets.
Only resume normal use after the authority officially lifts the notice and follow any flushing instructions.

articles.title: Home utility shutoff reference
articles.summary: Document household utility controls before an emergency.
body: Locate the main water shutoff, electrical service disconnect, and gas meter or shutoff without operating them unnecessarily.
Photograph or sketch each location and record access instructions in a protected household reference.
Ask the utility or a qualified professional which controls occupants may safely operate and under what conditions.
Never approach damaged electrical equipment, standing water near electrical service, or suspected gas leaks to operate a control.
If you smell gas or suspect a leak, leave the area and contact the gas utility or emergency services from a safe location. Do not operate electrical switches or create sparks.
Only qualified personnel or the utility should restore gas service after a shutoff.
Update the reference after repairs, renovations, or changes to utility equipment.

articles.title: Radio communications message log
articles.summary: Record radio traffic accurately during emergency support activities.
body: Prepare a paper log with columns for date, local time, station or sender, recipient, message summary, and action taken.
Identify the radio service and follow applicable licensing, frequency, and operational requirements.
Listen before transmitting and use concise plain language unless an authorized procedure specifies otherwise.
Record callsigns and message details accurately. Ask for repetition when critical information is unclear.
Distinguish confirmed information from unverified reports and record the source of each report.
Avoid transmitting unnecessary personal, medical, or sensitive information over open radio channels.
Mark tasks completed and retain logs according to the incident organization’s procedures.

articles.title: Floodwater exposure precautions
articles.summary: Reduce avoidable hazards when floodwater is present.
body: Stay out of floodwater whenever possible. Floodwater may conceal debris, sewage, sharp objects, and energized equipment.
Do not drive through flooded roads. Turn around and choose a safe alternative route.
Follow local evacuation orders and avoid entering damaged buildings until officials indicate it is safe.
Keep children and pets away from standing floodwater and contaminated materials.
If contact with floodwater occurs, wash exposed skin with soap and clean water as soon as possible and cover wounds with waterproof dressings.
Seek medical advice promptly for injuries, signs of infection, or significant exposure involving an open wound.
Never touch downed power lines or electrical equipment in or near floodwater.

articles.title: Emergency sanitation station
articles.summary: Set up a temporary hand hygiene and waste management area during a disruption.
body: Choose a location separated from food preparation and drinking water storage.
Use clean running water and soap for handwashing when available. If unavailable, use an appropriate alcohol based hand sanitizer when hands are not visibly dirty.
Provide a covered trash container and liners, and keep waste inaccessible to children, animals, and pests.
For toilet interruptions, follow local public health and emergency management instructions for approved temporary sanitation arrangements.
Never discharge untreated waste into streams, wells, storm drains, or drinking water sources.
Wear appropriate protection when handling contaminated waste and wash hands afterward.
Inspect the station daily for leaks, overflowing containers, and contamination.

articles.title: Family evacuation departure checklist
articles.summary: Use a repeatable departure sequence when an evacuation is ordered or necessary.
body: Confirm the evacuation order, hazard area, recommended routes, and destination using official local information.
Account for every household member and arrange assistance for anyone with mobility, medical, or communication needs.
Take essential medications, identification, emergency contact information, assistive equipment, and available go bags.
Check vehicle fuel or charge, accessible transport options, road conditions, and a backup route before leaving.
Notify a trusted contact of the destination and expected check in method when doing so is safe.
Leave immediately when conditions require it. Do not delay for nonessential belongings or routine property preparations.
Follow official instructions and do not return until authorities indicate it is safe.
